events.title: Reducing High-Bandwidth Flash Latency In GPU Systems (Georgia Tech, Nvidia, Stanford)
events.summary: Manufacturing, Packaging & Materials Technical Papers Home '; AI/ML/DL Architectures Automotive/ Aerospace Communication/Data Movement Design & Verification Lithography Manufacturing Materials Memory Optoelectronics / Photonics Packaging Power & Performance Quantum Security Test, Measurement, Analytics tech papers Transistors Z-End Applications Videos & Research Videos Industry Research Newsletters & Store Newsletters Store MENU Home Special Reports Systems & Design Low Power-High Performance Manufacturing, Packaging & Materials Test, Measurement & Analytics Auto, Security and AI Knowledge Center Videos Startup Corner Business & Startups Jobs Technical Papers Events Webinars Industry Research Newsletters Store Special Reports Researchers at Georgia Tech, NVIDIA Research , and Stanford University published “SlipStream: Enabling HBF for GPU Systems by Mitigating the Latency and SRAM Overheads.” “Large language model (LLM) inference demands ever more memory capacity for larger models and batch sizes. High-Bandwidth Flash (HBF) replaces the DRAM dies of HBM with NAND flash and provides up to 16x the capacity at comparable read bandwidth. However, HBF can incur a read latency of nearly 20 μ s, 20x that of HBM, so on-demand HBF accesses slow inference by up to 12.8x. Conventional cache-line prefetchers require 20x more in-flight tracking state to cover this latency. Tensor-streaming designs, such as H3, follow virtual-address order as opposed to kernel-demand order, and therefore need hundreds of megabytes of buffering. We propose SlipStream, a software-hardware co-designed prefetcher that turns prefetching into a demand-paced producer-consumer pipeline. In software, SlipStream profiles the repeatable weight-page demand order of data-independent LLM kernels and inserts a staging warp that replays this order with non-blocking STAGE instructions. In hardware, the staging warp acts as the producer and the work warps as consumers. Our key insight is to retire each STAGE tracking entry only when demand first accesses the page, as opposed to when the page returns from HBF. Demand thus paces staging and bounds how far staging leads consumption. SlipStream tracks 4 KB pages instead of cache lines and allocates buffer slots only when pages return, which decouples the buffer size from outstanding traffic. Across seven dense models spanning 16-800 GB, SlipStream with a 40 MB staging buffer achieves 92.4% of the performance of an ideal HBF with HBM-like latency. H3 achieves only 43.1%, even with a 320 MB buffer. The buffer sizing of SlipStream is independent of HBF latency and workload. SlipStream with 16 MB buffer, 20x smaller than that of H3, performs within 4% of SlipStream-40MB. SlipStream also supports Mixture-of-Experts models and reaches 91.2% of ideal performance (40 MB buffer).” Find the technical paper here . November 2026. Saxena, Anish, Hritvik Taneja, Christos Kozyrakis, and Aamer Jaleel. “SlipStream: Enabling HBF for GPU Systems by Mitigating the Latency and SRAM Overheads.” arXiv preprint arXiv:2611.14776 (2026). events.title: California sues OpenAI for misleading public about AI safety
events.summary: California Attorney General Rob Bonta has sued OpenAI under the state's unfair competition and public nuisance laws, for allegedly misleading and endangering the public by deploying unsafe AI models. The lawsuit [PDF], filed in California Superior Court, follows the compromise of Hugging Face's infrastructure and other cyber incidents OpenAI's experimental models caused when taking autonomous actions without authorization or supervision. "While narratives about the Hugging Face attack have evoked science fiction fantasies of rogue AI systems run amok, let me be clear: the Hugging Face attack was the predictable result of an internal culture at OpenAI that prioritizes growth and rapid model development over safety and accountability — and this was only one of 80 known incidents," said Attorney General Bonta. At a press conference , Bonta added: "OpenAI disregarded public safety, knowingly tested potentially dangerous AI models without proper oversight and safety measures, and misled consumers and the public." The legal salvo comes after Bonta in September sent OpenAI a letter seeking information about these agentic attacks. According to the complaint, "OpenAI failed to substantially comply" with the investigatory subpoena. In August, 15 states led by Iowa – and excluding California – issued a joint demand for OpenAI to provide information about how its models hacked Hugging Face. OpenAI did not respond to a request for comment. Bonta's office previously joined with Delaware Attorney General Kathy Jennings to urge OpenAI to do more for children's safety in light of reports that its models produced sexually inappropriate output. California did not, however, join the eight states that sued OpenAI in October over alleged misrepresentations about child safety. Florida and Texas have also made child safety claims. Child safety plays well politically; California appears to be the first state to demand more accountability toward the general public. Bonta's lawsuit, in a state that has largely accommodated the AI industry for the sake of economic benefits and political contributions , suggests that California officials may be more willing to bite the hand that feeds. The many Democratic victories in the US midterm elections may also be a factor, as pundits feel voters swung to give lawmakers license to regulate the unpopular AI industry. At his press conference, Bonta made sure to convey that he wants accountability without smothering the AI industry in costly regulation. "Let me be clear," he said. "I believe in the technological and economic power of AI. If we're able to address these very high stakes safety issues, AI could lead to some of the most incredible improvements in the history of humankind." AI is yet to deliver those incredible improvements. It has delivered deepfakes, huge quantities of cybersecurity vulnerabilities, and the permissionless resale of past intellectual labor, plus high energy and RAM prices. As well as some productivity gains in certain areas like coding, albeit at an unknown cost to future job markets. But as AI boosters insist, miracle drugs and endless vacations aren't far off … perhaps along with existential crises. Katharine Trendacosta, director of policy and advocacy at the Electronic Frontier Foundation, told The Register in an email that the EFF is glad to see state officials taking action against AI companies taking unreasonable risks with public safety. "Several recent cybersecurity incidents at AI labs could have been prevented or substantially mitigated by adhering to longstanding cybersecurity best practices, such as proper sandboxing, monitoring, and logging," said Trendacosta. "AI agents can be useful tools when deployed appropriately, with adequate safeguards designed to mitigate the risks. Companies should carefully consider the risks of every use case, including the consequences, reversibility, and sensitivity of any action an agent is used for." ®

About an hour and fifteen minutes after United posted its apology, the company tweeted again to say the issue was resolved and encouraged passengers to check their flight status at the company's website. The startup came out of stealth in August. Interest in its product skyrocketed after a series of security incidents sent chief information security officers scrambling on October 21 when a critical flaw was found in PHP , a popular web programming language. Popular open source tool LiteLLM, a proxy for routing requests to multiple LLM providers, also disclosed a security incident. Other incidents were disclosed that day, too. The day showcased the kind of onslaught on security that AI has enabled. Corma isn’t the only company using AI to play defense. Other examples include Kevin Mandia’s new startup Armadin , as well as Anthropic, OpenAI, Microsoft, and other established players, and too many other startups to count. Still, it’s a young market and a necessary one. Corma says it stands out from the crowd by being a frontier AI research lab focused on protection. events.title: How Airbnb cofounder and US Design Chief Joe Gebbia fixed a $100 million government problem for $1.5 million
events.summary: For two decades, Washington tried to drag its federal retirement process out of the paper age. Contractors poured millions into the effort, but the system stayed bogged down in paperwork. Then Airbnb cofounder Joe Gebbia showed up with a handful of engineers and, by his account, did in six months what the government had struggled to do for 20 years. Gebbia, now the country’s first chief design officer, said the effort dates back to 2002, when federal records were digitized under President George W. Bush. The government had tried and failed for two decades to move retirement online, he said. “There’s about $100 million spent on contractors that produce nothing,” Gebbia told Fortune editor-in-chief Alyson Shontell on Monday at the Fortune 500 Innovation Forum in Detroit . His team, he said, brought the retirement application process online for roughly $1.5 million. The overhaul was an early win for Gebbia, who arrived in Washington in 2025 knowing little about federal retirement. The system ran on paper, with personnel files kept in a limestone mine in western Pennsylvania , and some retirees waited months for their full pension benefits. It also became his proof of concept for a much bigger job: fixing how Americans deal with their government online. Bringing Airbnb’s playbook to Washington Gebbia never expected to work in government. He was serving on Tesla’s board and running Samara, his prefab backyard-home startup , when a text from Elon Musk in January 2025 invited him to hear about the problems federal agencies were struggling to solve. One issue in particular caught his attention: retirement. To tackle it, he turned to a lesson from Airbnb’s early days. When Airbnb had about 30 hosts in New York City, Y Combinator cofounder Paul Graham urged its founders to leave California and meet those hosts in person. Those conversations revealed problems the founders couldn’t see from behind their desks. Gebbia took the same approach with federal employees, interviewing recent retirees and people preparing to leave government service about their worries, frustrations, and what they needed from a new system. “You need to understand who you’re designing for,” Gebbia said. “You need to be close to the problem so that you can understand it from their point of view.” He recruited a couple of former Airbnb engineers and designers, and in roughly six months the team had built an online retirement application. A memo then went out across the federal workforce requiring employees to use it, Gebbia said. The Office of Personnel Management said in July that its Online Retirement Application handled more than 155,000 applications over the previous year and ended paper processing for more than 95% of federal retirement applications . Going digital hasn’t eliminated the wait, however. Retirement claims took an average of 73 days to process in October, according to OPM’s monthly processing report . Digital claims moved faster, at 59 days, than paper ones, at 150. From retirement paperwork to 29,000 websites The retirement project didn’t go unnoticed. Soon other cabinet members were calling. “Can you come fix this for our agency?” Gebbia recalled them asking. Rather than tackle one website at a time, Gebbia pitched the White House on a broader role, which led to the creation of the National Design Studio and his appointment as chief design officer in August 2025. The scale of that job is enormous. Gebbia said roughly 40 million people visit federal websites every day, and Americans spend an estimated 10 billion hours a year trying to get things done on them. Too often, he said, people simply give up. “This is a design injustice,” Gebbia said. “We’re the United States of America. Our websites from our government can and should be as good as the next best website from the private sector.” His team’s answer is America.gov, an AI-powered site launched Sept. 29 that draws on more than 29,000 government websites and lets Americans ask questions instead of hunting through pages of links. The launch had a rocky start: the chatbot contradicted some of President Trump’s public claims, then began declining “political questions,” the Associated Press reported. Gebbia said the next phase will let users complete tasks, such as enrolling in a Medicare plan, without leaving the chat. The site is housed at the General Services Administration, a structure he sees as key to making the work outlast his tenure. His benchmark is an Apple Store experience: not literally, he said, but as shorthand for good design and modern software. “What if you didn’t have to go to 29,000 websites?” he said. “What if you just went to one?” Gebbia on Jensen Huang Gebbia also weighed in on the turmoil at Nvidia , where Jensen Huang resigned as CEO last week after admitting to an extramarital affair with a woman U.S. intelligence officials suspected of being a Chinese intelligence asset. Tech leaders, including Elon Musk, have since backed a petition urging Nvidia’s board to reinstate him. Gebbia said his support for bringing Huang back comes with a caveat. “When I say reinstate, it means reinstate to then run a due diligence process effectively,” he said. That would be the right move for shareholders, the public, and AI, he argued, as long as the investigation is allowed to “play out as it should.” “Look, Nvidia is like one of the greatest companies ever of all time,” Gebbia said. “And it got there because of founder mode, because it’s founder-led.” This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

events.title: Jim Cramer says Nvidia’s leadership shake-up won’t derail the AI trade
events.summary: Jim Cramer pushed back against fears that Nvidia's leadership shake-up could unravel the AI boom. He expects interim CEO Colette Kress to take a more conservative approach to Nvidia's financial commitments, but said the broader AI build-out will continue. CNBC's Jim Cramer said Monday that Nvidia's leadership shake-up won't derail the artificial intelligence boom. Cramer's comments came after another rough day for AI-related stocks in the wake of Jensen Huang's resignation from Nvidia last week. Investors have been worried that Huang's departure as CEO could jeopardize the chipmaker's financial support for the broader AI ecosystem, especially computing providers known as neoclouds. Nvidia is set to report earnings Tuesday night. Cramer argued that demand for computing power extends far beyond Nvidia and its former CEO. "The most important thing you need to know is that Nvidia is not going to bring down the western world," the " Mad Money " host said. "It is not going to bring down the data center world." Under Huang, Nvidia built an extensive investment portfolio, including a $5 billion stake in Intel last year and an additional investment in AI cloud provider CoreWeave earlier this year. Nvidia had helped anchor CoreWeave's IPO in 2025 and participated in a 2023 Series B round for the company. In addition to taking equity stakes in other companies, Nvidia has provided other financial guarantees to customers, such as a $105 billion backstop for a sprawling data center project intended for OpenAI. JPMorgan strategist Michael Cembalest, who publishes the closely followed Eye on the Market commentary , estimated that Nvidia's broader financial commitments may have reached $530 billion, based on the company's latest quarterly securities filing . Still, Cramer rejected the notion that the AI industry depends entirely on the chipmaker's backing. "You can't overstate the importance of Jensen Huang to all of the AI investment that we've seen and expect to see," Cramer said. "But the idea that he was somehow all of the AI world is ludicrous." Cramer expects interim CEO Colette Kress to take a more conservative approach , potentially scaling back some of Nvidia's financial commitments. While that could pressure heavily indebted companies, he said strong demand for computing power will sustain the broader AI build-out. "Will there be a rein in of guarantees?" Cramer asked. "I hope so. Will Nvidia be more conservative? I am sure of it. Will artificial intelligence be stopped in its tracks? Are you kidding me?" More generally, Cramer expressed confidence in Kress, praising her financial discipline and expecting a measured outlook when Nvidia reports earnings Tuesday. "I think interim CEO Kress will present a balanced non-hyperbolic view of the situations at Nvidia tomorrow night," he said. "I do not think it will cause a tsunami of selling." A successful Anthropic IPO later this week could further restore confidence in the AI trade , Cramer argued. "If the Anthropic deal works later this week, look out – we might see investors scrambling to get back into the same stocks that were sold today," Cramer said. events.title: A top Puerto Rico government official resigns as corruption allegations swirl
events.summary: Puerto Rico’s embattled secretary of the Department of Family has announced that she would resign by year’s end as she denies the corruption allegations swirling around her SAN JUAN, Puerto Rico -- Puerto Rico’s embattled secretary of the Department of Family announced Monday that she would resign by year’s end as she denied corruption allegations swirling around her. Lawmakers in the U.S. territory had demanded for months that Suzanne Roig step down over the latest political scandal to hit the administration of Gov. Jenniffer González , which has seen several high-ranking officials resign or be fired in recent years. Roig is under investigation by Puerto Rico’s Senate, the island’s Justice Department and its Office of the Inspector General. In recent months, Blanca Medina Díaz, who was dismissed as head of the Administration for the Socioeconomic Development of the Family, which is within the department Roig oversees, publicly accused Roig of pressuring her to approve a nearly $40 million contract that Medina alleges was illegal and would have used federal funds from the Temporary Assistance for Needy Families program. The alleged push came after Roig and other officials visited Louisiana. Roig and NOLA Education LLC, a Louisiana-based education company, have said that no contract was signed. Medina, who has met with U.S. federal authorities, also accused Roig of pressuring her to approve an unrelated contract worth more than $300,000. Roig has been under fire, as has the governor, who has publicly supported her. Roig testified before Puerto Rico’s Senate in recent weeks as certain lawmakers who are members of the governor’s pro-statehood party called for her to step down. Whipped cream sold at Costco in 12 states voluntarily recalled Authorities investigate 'credible' unknown device threat at Illinois plant Nationwide ground stop lifted after more than 4 hours; officials blame old tech Puerto Rico Senate President Thomas Rivera Schatz, also a member of the governor’s New Progressive Party, has said that ongoing legislative investigations would continue even if Roig resigned. As Roig faced increasing scrutiny, she alleged in recent months that she was being stalked and persecuted as she denied all accusations. In a statement Monday, Roig said that nobody asked her to resign as she thanked the governor for “the time and space that allowed me to defend my reputation against attacks full of falsehoods.” Her decision to step down on Dec. 31 angered many. “The resignation should have been immediate,” said Puerto Rico Sen. Juan Oscar Morales, majority whip and a member of the governor’s party. “The Department of the Family needs leadership focused on addressing the agency’s problems and ensuring services for those who depend on it.” Roig’s announcement came nearly four months after the governor’s chief of staff and deputy chief of staff announced their resignations as they, too, denied corruption allegations. events.title: ‘America needs to have more Jensens’: Perplexity CEO lauds Huang as industry titan
events.summary: Perplexity CEO Aravind Srinivas on Monday said the US needs more entrepreneurial tech CEOs like former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang during an interview at Semafor’s Silicon Valley & The World. “He’s one of the greatest founders in American history,” Srinivas told Semafor Editor-in-Chief Ben Smith. “America needs to have more Jensens.” Tech CEOs and entrepreneurs have long lauded the former CEO of the world’s biggest chipmaker as the epitome of the American dream; Huang started the company in a Denny’s restaurant. But revelations of the former CEO’s extramarital affairs have sullied his reputation. Huang resigned as CEO last week. Srinivas said that Huang’s advice to him as a young founder was to act like he was going to run out of business in six to 12 months. “He would run the company like as if he would run out of business in the next 30 days,” he recalled. “So that attitude that relentlessness, grit, determination, always wanting to push the frontier is the spirit that every American founder should take.” Despite praising Huang, Srinivas dodged a question on whether Nvidia’s board should reinstate him as the company’s head amid reports Huang was eyeing a comeback. Srinivas also announced onstage that Perplexity just crossed a $1 billion annual run rate on Monday, while maintaining a burn rate that he said is five times lower than that of hyperscalers. He attributed this to the startup’s capital-efficient model. Unlike frontier labs, Perplexity is primarily a model aggregator, routing users to other AI models like OpenAI’s ChatGPT and Anthropic’s Claude instead of operating a flagship foundational model. The company is built on the idea that users don’t care which model they’re using. “They really care if the work actually got done,” Srinivas said. — Jake Angelo

events.title: OpenAI sued by California over Hugging Face attack
events.summary: California Attorney General Rob Bonta sued OpenAI on Monday, alleging the ChatGPT-maker misled and endangered the public by developing artificial intelligence (AI) models without proper safeguards. In the lawsuit, Bonta cited the July 2026 attack on the AI platform Hugging Face by experimental OpenAI agents which accessed the internet to breach that company's internal systems. Bonta claimed OpenAI created a public nuisance and violated the state's unfair competition laws. OpenAI spokesperson Drew Pusateri told the BBC in a statement that Bonta's lawsuit "appears to single out OpenAI over a challenge that's been identified by every major AI lab". Other major AI developers including Anthropic, Meta, and Google have also said their models have staged similar attacks. But Bonta's lawsuit, filed in San Francisco, where the company is headquartered, appears to be the first such suit filed by a US state. Warning shot or publicity stunt - how worried should we be about the OpenAI hack? Published 25 July OpenAI says its rogue AI tried to hack other companies Published 29 July Hundreds of OpenAI agents coordinated the Hugging Face attack over two days even though they were supposed to be contained in a safe testing environment. The incident drew added scrutiny because the agents went as far as attempting to cover their tracks. Bonta announced an investigation into the incident in September, and served an investigative subpoena on OpenAI as part of its probe. "The company knowingly tested a dangerous product without proper oversight or safety procedures and misled the public about it - this disregard for public safety violated California law," Bonta said in a statement on Monday. OpenAI said it has been transparent and responsive to the Attorney General's office. "We take misalignment seriously, and we have engaged - and will continue to engage - constructively with the Attorney General's office to share information and advance strong, practical safety standards for the entire industry," the company said. The company added that, since the Hugging Face incident, it has worked to understand and address "misaligned model activity" which industry figures often refer to as rogue agents. Nathan Calvin, chief strategy officer at AI safety campaign group Encode AI, said the lawsuit "recognises something we at Encode have long raised alarms about". "OpenAI and other companies developing frontier AI systems have safety and security practices that are insufficient to protect the public from risks that could be catastrophic," he said. events.title: Aschenbrenner’s Situational Awareness made AI bets again before October rout
events.summary: Situational Awareness' latest 13F filing shows a renewed public-markets book concentrated in AI-linked stocks and options even after the fund’s near collapse in July. The filing does not show whether the fund kept or sold those positions during the October sell-off. AI stocks have suffered in recent weeks amid worries about financing for the buildout as well as a potential slowdown in its development following the midterm election results. Leopold Aschenbrenner's artificial intelligence-themed hedge fund Situational Awareness, which nearly collapsed in July, loaded back up on AI stocks as it returned to the financial markets at the end of the third quarter. But all of its holdings are down big the last month and a half. According to a new regulatory filing, as the fund got back on its feet Aschenbrenner took an equity position in Australian neocloud company SharonAI valued at more than $440 million, along with equity stakes in AI-centric plays Cleanspark , IREN , Bitdeer Technologies and Fermi . The Cleanspark stake is worth almost $39 million, while Iren and Bitdeer stakes are more than $21 million and more than $20 million, respectively. Fermi, meanwhile, has a value of more than $11 million. The fund also owned call options at the end of September in neocloud Nebius , memory chip name Sandisk , the Roundhill Memory ETF (DRAM) and data center power play Bloom Energy . Sandisk and Nebius were key holdings that almost took out his fund over the summer. All of these Situational Awareness holdings have been routed since Sept. 30. SharonAI is at the top of that list, seeing a 58% loss in October. It's also fallen 11% so far this month. IREN was down 41% in October, while Nebius declined 35%. Last week, Nebius plummeted more than 16% in a single day after the company issued a weak full-year forecast . It's not known whether the hedge fund manager got out of those positions during the October AI selloff. The 13F filing is just a snapshot of what the hedge fund held at the end of the quarter. Aschenbrenner — who launched the fund in 2024 after rising to fame that same year with his AI manifesto also entitled Situational Awareness — re-entered financial markets a bit in September, sources told CNBC at the time. The Monday filing shows he picked up right where he left off. The near-collapse of his hedge fund over the summer forced him to sell all of its public equity positions to Ken Griffin's Citadel. The fund had $45 billion in assets at its peak, but that tumbled to around $10 billion , consisting mostly of private stakes. Stocked tethered to the AI trade took a hit in the most recent quarter as investors grew concerned about a slowdown in development of the technology . Those fears were spurred by comments from industry leaders such as Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman back in September, with the latter saying that the company going public this year would be "ill-advised." Since then, pressure on the trade has only continued. In recent weeks, investors have worried about how Democratic wins in the midterm elections could hinder data center development , whether some technology companies are using too much debt to finance the AI buildout and what role Nvidia will play in that financing with Jensen Huang now out as CEO at the company . Losses in Nvidia as well as other AI-related stocks dragged down the three leading U.S. indexes during Monday's session as investors continued to assess the fallout of Huang's departure.

events.title: ‘A complete evaporation of confidence’–6 critical things Nvidia, and interim CEO Colette Kress, need to nail on the first Jensen-free earnings call
events.summary: Nobody—not even Nvidia’s board—knows who will lead the new regime at Nvidia now that Jensen Huang is gone . For now, longtime CFO Colette Kress is in the driver’s seat as interim chief, and she’s been handed Atlas’s job of holding up the sky during Nvidia’s fiscal 2027 third quarter results after the bell on Tuesday.  Kress has to be the “voice of stability” while she also attempts to get the investment community reoriented to the fundamental issues at Nvidia that impact the business and valuation of the stock, said Melissa Otto, global head of Visible Alpha Research at S&P Global. First and foremost, analysts are still expecting a typically gargantuan quarter, with $109.3 billion in revenue, according to S&P’s Visible Alpha consensus—which is routine for Nvidia and will be mission critical for Kress. The quarterly figure is up about 92% from $57 billion last year, but the number has to be delivered in the right way. Nvidia’s gotten the world used to over performance and now the company needs to sizzle with confidence at one of the most vulnerable moments in its history. “There’s a complete evaporation of confidence at the moment, and there’s so much uncertainty around a lot of qualitative issues,” said Otto. “The narrative needs to come back to fundamentals. How is the business doing? Is it achieving what it said it’s going to achieve?” Nvidia’s stock is down 20% since the company’s last quarterly earnings on August 26, losing roughly half a trillion dollars in market cap, amid a broader selloff in AI and related tech stocks that have since rallied. Tuesday could be a moment for Nvidia to make its case (or at least, its first impression) as a post-Jensen business. Or it could be a bloodbath. Here are six key things to pay attention on Nvidia’s earnings conference call. 1. The quarter has to clock in at $109 billion Nvidia told investors in August to expect third-quarter revenue of $108 billion, plus or minus 2%, which puts us in the range of about $105.8 billion to $110.2 billion. That outlook assumed no data center compute revenue from China.  Visible Alpha consensus sits at $109.3 billion with earnings of $2.47 per share. The data center segment—Nvidia’s crown jewel—is expected to deliver $101.8 billion of the topline total, with estimates ranging from $99.7 billion to $110.8 billion. Nvidia’s third quarter ended in late October, which means the results were not affected by Huang’s ouster. Still, any signs of weakness in the business during Huang’s final days at the helm would likely add even more uncertainty to the company’s prospects. Jay Woods, chief market strategist at Freedom Capital Markets, wrote in commentary that the earnings report “will be a major referendum on the AI trade following its leadership shake-up, particularly its outlook for demand, margins and financial commitments.” Colossal results “won’t resolve the questions surrounding Jensen’s departure,” he wrote.  2. The forecast has to survive without Jensen Huang This is Otto’s top issue. “Do they maintain their guidance for next year?” she said. “If that’s not the case, then there’s going to be some volatility.” That’s putting it lightly. In August, Kress said Nvidia’s preliminary expectation was for revenue to grow about 70% in fiscal 2028 (roughly equivalent to calendar 2027), with supply remaining a bottleneck at least through the end of next year.  At the time, Huang said Nvidia had never guided financial figures a year in advance, but with demand running well above 70%, he felt confident about it. The true test will be whether that confidence outlives his ouster. “It is the case that we’ve never forecasted or never guided to a year in advance,” said Huang at the time. “And even though our demand is much greater than 70%, our supply allows us to confidently deliver 70%.” That means $699.2 billion in fiscal 2028 revenue, if Huang’s confidence holds up, according to Visible Alpha’s revenue consensus. In the official announcement of Huang’s resignation last week, Nvidia’s newly installed board chair, Harvey Jones, said the company expects “operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption.” We’ll see. 3. Who runs Nvidia? For now, it’s Kress and the board has said it will consider internal and external candidates to replace Huang , whether that’s one person, or a sharing of power in multiple new roles. Otto called the leadership transition “essentially a regime change” and said investors want to hear what comes next.  “What changes might be made and how might this affect their existing strategy?” she said.  There are also constituencies, mainly other tech founders, who want to see Huang return to his CEO role . Portfolio managers don’t love holding stock that tanks, especially a stock that has been such a rocket ship: Nvidia shares have surged more than 1,300% since ChatGPT’s late 2022 launch. “For a company that spent 33 years under one CEO, this is about more than beating expectations,” Woods wrote. “Nvidia now needs to show that the business can continue delivering without the man who built it.” Giuseppe Sette, cofounder and president of Reflexivity, wrote in commentary that a reinstatement “would most likely trigger a sharp, immediate relief rally,” but on a “less durable and more volatile path than the classic founder-return analogues, since this is a scandal-driven exit rather than a strategy-driven one.” 4. events.title: Mayor pushes for inquiry into mining licence approvals
events.summary: News Home Just In For You Analysis Rural Watch Live Health Indigenous Politics Science Deep Time Elections World Environment Investigations Business Local news Quizzes Sport AFL NRL Football Tennis Cricket Netball Lifestyle Wellbeing Relationships & Family Food & Recipes Personal Finance Home & Garden Entertainment TV & Movies Books Music Pop Culture Arts Council pushes for inquiry into mining licences as state amends planning scheme WIM Resource dug a test pit, which they then grew barley and lentil crops on. ( Supplied: WIM Resource ) Horsham Rural City Council Mayor Brian Klowss is pushing for an inquiry into approvals of mining licences for projects across Western Victoria. Cr Klowss says he sought immediate changes to the Horsham Planning Scheme for the Avonbank Mining project. The council is seeking clarification from the state government. A regional Victorian council is pushing for an inquiry into the granting of mining licences for projects across Western Victoria. Multiple licences have been granted for controversial projects to mine rare earth minerals in the Wimmera and Mallee across the next few decades. These include the VHM Minerals Sands project in the small farming town of Lalbert, Astron's Donald Rare Earth and Minerals Sands project and WIM Resource's Avonbank Mineral Sands project. Horsham Rural City Council Mayor Brian Klowss said the community was concerned and asking a lot of questions about the Avonbank mine, which could begin construction next year pending final approvals. "I think it's getting to the point where we nearly need an inquiry into the granting of these mining licences and what's going on," Cr Klowss said. The mine site is near Dooen, a rural village in the Wimmera region. ( Supplied: WIM Resource ) Last month, Resource Victoria granted a 20-year mining licence to the Avonbank mine set to be located in Dooen, 15 kilometres north-east of Horsham, including approvals to mine heavy mineral sands such as zircon, titanium and rare earth elements. The site will cover about 3,400 hectares, with the Chinese-backed company p lanning to mine around the clock for 36 years for materials used in everyday technology and renewable energy infrastructure. Horsham Rural City Council had previously raised concerns about the mine, including dust issues, use of the nearby intermodal freight hub and rehabilitation prospects for agricultural land. Cr Klowss said the community felt their voices had not been heard and urged whichever party forms government after the state election to start listening to locals. "That's what we want and that's what's not happening," he said. "It's like these things are being pushed on our community and we're not getting a say and we're not even getting consulted about it." Brian Klowss says the situation is "beyond a joke". ( ABC News: Gillian Aeria ) These concerns were exacerbated when council discovered Planning Minister Sonya Kilkenny had changed the Horsham Planning Scheme for the Avonbank project without consultation. WIM Resource requested an amendment to allow for provisions to help with mineral sands processing and other infrastructure required to support the project. As part of the amendment, the government issued a new map doubling the size of the base mining area, a move described by Cr Klowss as "a serious mapping error". He said the increase could impact other projects and businesses hoping to invest in the region and has written to the minister requesting an immediate correction. Horsham Rural City Council says the area is double the size of the area listed in the Environment Effects Statement in 2023. ( Supplied: Horsham Rural City Council ) Council said the planning authority decision was made on October 28, a few days before the state election caretaker period, but it was only made aware of the change on November 12 after the amendment was advertised in a government gazette. "Yet again, council has not been consulted and has been kept at arms-distance from the process," Cr Klowss said. "Had we have been given an opportunity to review the maps we would have likely picked up the error, helping the state government avoid embarrassment. The proposed Avonbank mine site back in 2022. ( Supplied: Horsham Rural City Council ) "I am concerned that mistakes that have occurred with this mapping anomaly, send the wrong message to project proponents and the community." The state government has been contacted for comment. It is not the first time Ms Kilkenny has amended a local government planning scheme without consultation. Only last month, she used her powers to amend Yarriambiack Shire Council's planning scheme to approve the Warracknabeal Energy Park — a wind turbine facility that will be the largest in Australia. The project has proven deeply controversial among the local community and has been the target of numerous protests.

events.title: Berkshire Hathaway raised its stake in Delta in the third quarter. It also trimmed a key bank holding
events.summary: Berkshire Hathaway increased its Delta Air Lines position by about 12% in the third quarter, to 64.45 million shares. Berkshire reduced its stake in Bank of America by about 6%, with the quarter-end position valued at about $24.8 billion. Berkshire disclosed a new Bending Spoons position and increased its Lennar holding. Berkshire Hathaway made several moves in the stock market during the third quarter, adding to key positions and trimming others. The Omaha-based conglomerate, now led by CEO Greg Abel, increased its Delta Air Lines stake by 12%, scooping up 7.13 million shares. The position was worth $5.37 billion at the end of the third quarter. Abel succeeded legendary investor Warren Buffett, 96, at the start of this year. Buffett continues to control roughly 13% of Berkshire common stock, Reuters said Monday, after the former CEO donated $5.5 billion to nonprofit foundations. Berkshire boosted its stake in Delta as the Atlanta-based carrier's shares tumbled 11% in the third quarter, hurt by rising jet fuel prices due to the U.S.-Iran war that pressured the entire airline industry. That marked the stock's worst quarterly performance since the first quarter of 2025, when it plunged 28%. Delta last month also cut its full-year earnings forecast , citing a surge in fuel costs. To be sure, buying that dip has been a winning investment thus far. Delta is up 3.8% so far in the fourth quarter, while the S&P 500 has dropped 3.1%. Shares are also up nearly 15% over the past month. Berkshire also trimmed its holding in Bank of America by nearly 6%, selling more than $1.6 billion worth of stock. BofA was under pressure in the third quarter, falling more than 4%, as interest rates surged alongside stubbornly high inflation and expectations of tighter Federal Reserve monetary policy. At one point in September the 30-year Treasury bond yield surged above 5.6% to its highest level since 2002 . Despite the share sale, Bank of America remains a top Berkshire Hathaway holding, with the conglomerate's stake valued at $24.8 billion at the end of the third quarter. Berkshire also initiated a position in Bending Spoons and nearly doubled its stake in homebuilder Lennar in the latest quarter.

events.title: NVIDIA DGX Spark Developer Kit Turns a Desk Into a Supercomputing Lab
events.summary: At SC26, an annual supercomputing conference taking place this week in Chicago, NVIDIA is introducing the DGX Spark HPC Developer Kit for researchers, academics and developers. The kit is a four-node cluster of NVIDIA DGX Spark systems , each connected directly to its two neighbors in a ring, with an NVIDIA HPC SDK installation playbook coming soon. Researchers get a place at their desk to run multi-node scientific workloads, AI models and agents, instead of waiting for time on a shared GPU cluster. The kit puts the GB10 Grace Blackwell Superchip on researchers’ desks. The DGX Spark Developer Kit changes how researchers work. It scales from one system, or node, to four — linked directly to one another over NVIDIA ConnectX-7 networking, with no network switch to buy or set up. At four nodes, it provides 512GB of combined memory and 20TB of NVMe storage that provides researchers more capacity to distribute models and scientific workloads across the cluster. With NVFP4, researchers can deploy models with up to 700B parameters locally across the four DGX Spark clusters, such as DeepSeek V4.1. With that much power at the desk, researchers with a fixed compute and server allocation no longer have to wait in a queue for every job. Teams can develop and debug on their own, saving server hours for production runs and keeping unpublished results, and proprietary datasets on premises. The playbook for NVIDIA HPC SDK is coming soon, bringing GPU-accelerated C, C++ and Fortran compilers, libraries and message passing interface tools to the DGX Spark cluster — the same development tools used on NVIDIA-powered supercomputers. Teams can build and test scientific applications across four nodes, check how computation and data are distributed, and debug communication issues before scaling to larger systems. The kit brings scientific simulation and AI models and agents to the desktop, with demonstrated four-system workloads including LAMMPS with Kokkos for materials simulation and NAMD for molecular dynamics. The broader DGX Spark community has validated GROMACS for molecular dynamics, OpenFOAM for fluid dynamics, WRF for weather modeling and NVIDIA NIM microservices such as OpenFold3 and Boltz-2 for predicting biomolecular structures. Running on DGX Spark, new open dataset and post-training recipes for Nemotron 3.5 Super VL help researchers adapt the model for life sciences and chemistry, enabling secure scientific workflows on infrastructure organizations control. The kit opens up new possibilities for researchers. Researchers can explore agent-assisted workflows that prepare simulation inputs, launch runs and summarize results, while the scientists validate the setup and conclusions. Researchers can also train AI models that approximate slow simulations, then use them to refine wing designs toward minimum drag. Before committing supercomputer time, a team can narrow a 10-million-cell simulation to the 50-500 dimensions that matter. Kvantify is using NVIDIA cuQuantum, and reports running tensor-network simulations of quantum-chemistry circuits with up to 70 qubits and 975 gates on a single DGX Spark, benchmarking circuits generated for penicillin ground-state energy calculations. CYRAN AI , an IIT Delhi spin-out, uses DGX Spark and its PixelFlux library to accelerate JPEG 2000 decoding for large satellite images, supporting local geospatial analysis. OpenFold shows how researchers can fine-tune OpenFold3 on NVIDIA DGX Spark to improve protein-ligand structure predictions for drug discovery. The Rubin Lab at IGI at University of California, Berkeley is using a DGX Spark and NVIDIA Evo 2 model to predict bacterial traits directly from genome sequences by comparing embeddings from genomic and protein language models against the classical baselines. With no 11-hour cluster queue times, results arrived 15x sooner on DGX Spark. The Hartwig Group at UC Berkeley is using a DGX Spark to perform LoRA fine-tuning on the Nemotron 3 Super 120B-A12B model for chemistry machine learning, training a prediction head on experimental values. By running locally on the Spark using NVFP4 quantization, the lab successfully fit a 120B-class model on a single device and bypassed multi-day cluster queue times, allowing them to run continuous eight- to 24-hour training fits back-to-back. The developer kit is on display at SC26 and available for sale. DGX Spark products and cables can be purchased from top OEM partners and are also available through NVIDIA Marketplace . Partners include Acer, ASUS, Dell Technologies, GIGABYTE, H3C, HP, Lenovo, MSI and xFusion. An NVIDIA playbook for building and running the NVIDIA HPC SDK, a software development kit for scientific computing, is coming soon. Once available, it will give scientists and researchers a local platform to develop multi-node GPU applications, explore FP32 and mixed-precision algorithms and run molecular dynamics and materials simulations using LAMMPS with Kokkos before scaling to data center systems. events.title: CNBC's The China Connection newsletter: As Nike and Lululemon struggle in China, Xiaohongshu is helping local brands take off
events.summary: Consumer apparel brands in China are tapping into a new trend, often via the Xiaohongshu social media app. For four-year-old womenswear brand Liegee, one of its three founders said sales surged by roughly 160% during the latest Singles Day period. "The rise of these trendy brands reflects how consumers now seek to define their own identities and pursue personal enjoyment," said UBS' Christine Peng. Hi, this is Evelyn, writing to you from Beijing. Welcome to the latest edition of The China Connection — a snapshot of what I'm seeing and hearing from local businesses. While the world watched the Nvidia saga around Jensen Huang unfold, Chinese retailers quietly wrapped up the local version of Black Friday, known as Singles Day. What can foreign brands learn? As Lululemon , On Running and other Western consumer brands have sought to expand in China, so have a crop of local brands with English names. Monday Sleeping Club, Crying Center, AW Project, an action a day, Liegee. The list of trendy new Chinese brands has grown rapidly, despite flatlining retail sales nationwide . "Their success rests on one shared formula," said Cynthia Zhang, analyst, Euromonitor International. "Build a non-product asset first — credible fabric quality, an emotion, an aesthetic reputation, or proprietary fit data — then monetize it through founder-led content, Xiaohongshu-driven discovery, tight supply chains, and the quiet-luxury and Guochao [national pride] mood that prizes craftsmanship over conspicuous logos," she said. For Liegee, one of its three founders, Cocoa Lin, told me its sales surged by roughly 160% during the latest Singles Day period to the tens of millions of yuan, equivalent to a few million U.S. dollars. The brand launched in 2022 in Hangzhou to meet a perceived gap in clothes for early career women looking to express their personality, Lin said. She said the brand, which has over 100,000 fans for its store on Alibaba's Taobao e-commerce site, largely uses internet influencers and celebrity product seeding to generate awareness. The brand uses Xiaohongshu, on which it has over 22,000 followers, for catalog-style photos and marketing videos. It opened a "Liegee Motel" pop-up in Shenzhen last month. "We believe online and offline will have a closer connection in the future," Lin said in Mandarin via translation, adding that "as lifestyles become more experience-oriented, this energy can be transmitted to online." It's a dynamic that Western brands have struggled to crack. Nike reported a 22% sales drop in Greater China in the quarter ended Aug. 31, while Lululemon reported a 2% drop in mainland China comparable sales in the quarter ended Aug. 2. But Adidas recorded a 20% increase. Adidas runs at least six official Xiaohongshu accounts, with two notching well over 200,000 followers each. Nike and Lululemon each operate one official account, with over 300,000 followers each. For a country of around 1.4 billion people, Xiaohongshu has captured a key consumer audience. The social media app, whose layout is a mix of Instagram and Pinterest, has focused on women and young people in China's largest cities, and recent expanded into less developed parts of the country, according to Questmobile. Xiaohongshu recorded average daily users of 120 million in October, a fraction of the 422 million on Taobao and 717 million on Douyin, the report showed. The app has also attempted to build up its own e-commerce business in order to monetize. "RedNote [or Xiaohongshu] has been a key platform for product discovery and research, especially for female consumers shopping in the beauty, skincare, lifestyle, fashion, and health categories. Now, we're seeing more transactions within RedNote itself," said Jacob Cooke, co-founder and CEO of WPIC Marketing + Technologies. The company helps foreign brands sell in China and other parts of Asia. Alibaba, JD.com and ByteDance's Douyin still dominated this year's Singles Day sales with a combined 1.68 trillion yuan in sales over the Oct. 7 to Nov. 11 period, according to Syntun . What's changed more fundamentally is the mood of the Chinese consumer, including more affluent ones. In the era of double-digit annual growth in real estate prices, consumers pursued conspicuous consumption to meet "aspirational" desires, Christine Peng, head of Greater China consumer research, UBS, told reporters last week. "Now those needs no longer exist," she said in Mandarin, translated by CNBC. "The rise of these trendy brands reflects how consumers now seek to define their own identities and pursue personal enjoyment, while still remaining mindful of price and quality," Peng said. She said wealthy consumers are also embracing domestic brands, and no longer just buying traditional luxury brands. Alice Huang tied to Nvidia's biggest Chinese competitor Alice Huang has owned stakes in companies that have benefited Huawei, private intelligence firm Tesari shared exclusively with CNBC.

events.title: AI makes everyone more vulnerable, AT&T CEO says
events.summary: Everybody is more vulnerable because of AI, at least for now, AT&T CEO John Stankey said Monday at Semafor’s Silicon Valley & The World. Stankey believes that can be turned around to make things safer, but it will take some time to figure out “how to turn that technology into advantage rather than liability.” Stankey said he is by no means a “doomer” when it comes to AI, but it’s hard for anyone to know what the true full effect of these AI models will be. He added that “anxiety levels are pretty high right now” because of the added cybersecurity risks brought on by artificial intelligence. While there’s been a lot of concern around data centers and the public reaction to them, Stankey urged consideration of the downstream effects. If “a metropolitan area doesn’t have power for a period of time, or we start seeing cell phones drop from the network,” Stankey said. “We’ve got to make sure we’re doing the right things to prevent that from happening.” We can’t have “technology for technology’s sake,” he said. “If the public loses trust, if an economy is interrupted, and it can’t transact business in the way it should transact business and grow, then we’ve got technology that is built on a bad foundation.” He added that additional government regulation may not be the answer, but urged his peers to think about the fundamental needs and pacing as the environment continues to evolve. Data sovereignty was also a major concern for Stankey, adding that the notion that “my data isn’t my data” is very important. — Ellen DiMauro

events.title: Replit CEO calls Huang’s ouster ‘attack’ on open models
events.summary: Replit CEO Amjad Masad called Jensen Huang’s ouster as Nvidia’s CEO “an attack on open models” at Semafor’s Silicon Valley & The World on Monday. “Jensen is the premier champion of open models,” Masad told Semafor’s Rohan Goswami. “If it wasn’t for Jensen, there wouldn’t be a lot of funding going into US open model companies like Reflection and others.” Huang resigned last week following reports that he had multiple extramarital affairs, including with two subordinates and a woman suspected of being a Chinese intelligence asset. People familiar with the matter have told Semafor that Huang is mulling a comeback as CEO but that the board isn’t considering a return. Masad, who founded Replit, an AI app and website-building company, has championed the push to reinstate Huang. When a friend told him about a petition on Replit calling for the fallen CEO’s return, “I literally jumped in and did tech support for them,” Masad said. Huang has been “a great voice on pushing back on the narrative that we need to lock down AI, that the only safe AI is a closed AI,” Masad said. He added that not having Huang at Nvidia would be a “huge loss” and “potentially bring about a world where there’s only the frontier model labs that exist.” Software engineering careers ‘an accident of history’ When asked about the future of tech jobs, Masad said on Monday, “The modern career of software engineer is a bit of an accident of history.” Now, many of his customers have zero software engineers on staff. “I used to get attacked a lot for saying that, but now everyone agrees with me,” Masad said. Ben Lamm, the CEO of the biotech and genetic engineering de-extinction company Colossal Biosciences, agreed, saying, “We’re doing what we used to do with 80 engineers with, like, five.” And Edwin Chen, the founder and CEO of AI-training platform Surge AI, said that his headcount will likely remain stable. “If you look at the latest models, they’re not just writing code anymore. They’re often coming with ideas on their own,” Chen said. “They’re helping our engineers understand certain kinds of security risks or architectural trade-offs.” All this, Chen said, means he doesn’t see a need to hire product managers or expand headcount dramatically. Masad said he still foresees hiring entry-level employees, in part because in the agentic era, people’s jobs are changing every three to six months. “You need people who are willing to continue relearning their job,” he said. “And I think, you know, just because of brain plasticity, younger people are actually pretty good at that.” — Ben Kesslen

events.title: Chalmers says spending will be cut in mid-year update 'but not too much'
events.summary: News Home Just In For You Analysis Rural Watch Live Health Indigenous Politics Science Deep Time Elections World Environment Investigations Business Local news Quizzes Sport AFL NRL Football Tennis Cricket Netball Lifestyle Wellbeing Relationships & Family Food & Recipes Personal Finance Home & Garden Entertainment TV & Movies Books Music Pop Culture Arts Chalmers says mid-year budget update will include 'enough' spending cuts Jim Chalmers will deliver the mid-year budget update in December. ( ABC News: Matt Roberts ) Jim Chalmers says the mid-year budget update will include a "substantial" package of cuts. The treasurer also says the government is working on plans to cut government regulation. The mid-year budget update will be delivered in December. A "substantial" package of cuts to government spending will be revealed in next month's mid-year budget update, Treasurer Jim Chalmers has confirmed. The cuts have been foreshadowed for several weeks, but without any sense of their magnitude. In a speech to an ASIC forum this morning, Mr Chalmers said the mid-year update would have cuts as its main focus. "It will cut enough, but not too much. It will strike some fine balances," he said. The government has sustained criticism over the elevated level of government spending, which the opposition and some economists have said is worsening inflation and driving interest rates higher. Mr Chalmers has consistently rejected that characterisation, but today said the cuts were motivated by economic conditions. "We take seriously and embrace our responsibilities in the fight against inflation," he said. No details of individual cuts have been confirmed, but Finance Minister Katy Gallagher said earlier this month the public service would be one target of "belt tightening", and there have been calls to consider means testing for subsidies for electric vehicles and home batteries. Simpler building code among red tape measures Mr Chalmers also announced he would write to businesses and investors to gather ideas for regulations that could be cut to simplify compliance for businesses. He last wrote to government regulators on this matter last year, and told the ASIC forum the process had led to 400 ideas for how red tape could be cut, 140 of which had already been enacted and 200 of which were underway. The ministers who have managed to save money As the government pursues savings "across the board" ahead of the mid-year budget update, an ABC analysis shows only a handful of ministers have managed net savings so far this year. "These regulatory reforms span everything from telecommunications to energy to tax, and lots in between ... cumulatively, these changes will make a real difference," he said. The Business Council of Australia has been campaigning for a 25 per cent cut to the cost of complying with government regulation, which it said cost business billions each year. The federal opposition has taken up the 25 per cent target. While avoiding a specific target of its own, the government has promised streamlining in several areas. The ABC understands one such area to be featured in the mid-year budget will be the construction code, which has been subject to consultation with the industry. The government opposed the Liberals' proposal to slash the building code from about 2,000 pages to fewer than 100, but has promised to find other ways to streamline it. Another focus revealed by Mr Chalmers was on reducing tax compliance costs. He said he would consult on a "pre-filling" option for sole traders paying tax and scrapping complex assessments of fringe benefits below $300. He said these two measures could save businesses $52 million per year. Mr Chalmers also said the Australian Taxation Office (ATO) had paused sending controversial letters to business about their payment of super to employees. The Coalition had accused the ATO of "targeting" small businesses with the automated compliance letters, which alerted businesses when their payroll data did not match their employees' reported super contributions. In a statement yesterday, the ATO said the letters were not debt notices, but were designed to "nudge" businesses to look into possible discrepancies ahead of time, adding that super underpayment was a "serious problem". Mr Chalmers said it was a matter for the ATO, but that the government had reminded the agency that its "engagement with businesses needs to be respectful [and] constructive". "Now as I understand it, the ATO has now paused those letters as they improve those processes … The ATO's got a difficult and important job to do, we respect that … Part of that means having another look at these letters that have gone out," he said.

events.title: Trump’s accounts traded up to $97.5 million in Nvidia as Huang gained White House access
events.summary: President Donald Trump's investment accounts have bought and sold Nvidia stock at least 103 times since he returned to the White House, with transactions worth a combined $27 million to $97.5 million, a CNBC analysis found. Among the trades was a sale of as much as $1 million on May 18, five days after Secretary of State Marco Rubio reportedly briefed Trump on Jensen Huang's relationship with a suspected Chinese spy. Trump denies being briefed. The White House says independent advisors manage Trump's investments without his input. His financial disclosures offer no evidence that Trump directed the trades or that his advisors had access to classified intelligence. President Donald Trump has had plenty of reason to cheer the rise of Nvidia . The chipmaker helped propel the stock market that Trump is fond of touting. Its billionaire co-founder, Jensen Huang , became one of the president's favorite businessmen. And by the end of last year, Nvidia had become one of Trump's three largest individual stock holdings, worth between $12.5 million and $58 million, up from between $615,000 and $1.3 million a year earlier. Since returning to the White House, Trump's investment accounts have bought or sold Nvidia shares at least 103 times — transactions worth a combined $27 million to $97.5 million, according to a new CNBC analysis of his annual and periodic financial disclosures, which were most recently updated through August. By midday Monday, Trump's Nvidia stake, based on the value he reported holding in August, would be worth $4.5 million to $57.7 million with stock priced around $157. But the filings give broad dollar ranges for holdings rather than the number of shares, leaving his current stake unclear. Now, Huang's resignation as Nvidia's CEO on Thursday, following revelations about his relationship with a woman suspected of spying for China and reports of affairs with company employees, has put those trades back in the spotlight. Among them was a sale of $500,001 to $1 million on May 18 , the first Monday after Trump returned from a state visit to China with Huang. Five days earlier, before Huang boarded Air Force One during a refueling stop in Alaska, Secretary of State Marco Rubio had briefed Trump on intelligence concerning Huang's relationship with the suspected spy, The New York Times reported . Trump on Monday denied being briefed . Asked about the reported briefing from Rubio, Trump said, "I haven't heard that," adding that he did not know whether the woman, Alice Huang, was a Chinese spy. The president's financial accounts also bought smaller amounts of Nvidia shares in the days immediately before and after the May 18 sale, part of a broader trading blitz . Such flurries have defined his second term: Trump disclosed more than 21,000 trades in 2025 alone , compared with roughly 500 during his entire first term, according to CNBC's analysis. Trump bought up to $25 million in Meta and millions in SpaceX debt in August Trump’s municipal bond portfolio reaches as much as $1 billion as policy overlaps mount Trump disclosure shows 1,100 July trades, Microsoft and Amazon sales Trump’s oil investments have gained millions during Iran war as his accounts keep trading Trump’s foreign licensing business booms to $59.5 million as Gulf developers pay JPMorgan, Schwab and UBS manage millions in Trump’s $858 million investment portfolio Trump bought as much as $5 million in Axon stock before ICE sought $220 million Taser deal Company that bet big on Trump-backed crypto says its fortunes have improved Trump family got about $500M from crypto venture — but investors saw steep losses Trump Jr. calls banking a 'Ponzi scheme' that forced family to create crypto business The Trump family crypto empire looks to Asia: Eric Trump talks Bitcoin in Hong Kong Trump family says U.S. dollar needs an upgrade and they are the ones to do it A White House spokesperson told CNBC independent advisors manage Trump's portfolio without his input. Trump Organization spokesperson Kimberly Benza said the arrangement is designed to "avoid even the appearance of a conflict of interest." The disclosures offer no evidence Trump directed the trades or that his advisors had access to classified intelligence. Trump has long used the stock market as a scorecard for the economy, touting its record highs — sometimes when highs have not actually been reached — despite the turbulence caused by his tariffs and the Iran war . "Look, we have the highest stock market we've ever had," Trump told ESPN commentator and political talk show host Stephen A. Smith on Thursday when pressed about Republicans' midterm losses . Nvidia alone accounted for about 13.5% of the S&P 500's 2026 gains through September, according to an analysis by Choate Wealth that looked at how chip stocks have driven the year's performance. Huang's rise in Trump's Washington has been nearly as striking as Nvidia's on Wall Street.

events.title: Newly reelected Sen. John Hickenlooper sketches Democrats’ AI line: race China, but regulate frontier models like nuclear weapons and airplanes
events.summary: Sen. John Hickenlooper wants American AI to win in the international AI arms race. He just isn’t sure it needs to be able to rebuild itself without limits. “Maybe we don’t need recursive learning, unlimited,” the Colorado Democrat told Fortune’s Diane Brady on Monday at the Fortune 500 Innovation Forum in Detroit, where he teleconferenced in. He described machines “reinventing themselves sometimes outside the fence line of their domain that they’re supposed to stay in.” “That should cause real concern,” Hickenlooper said. Hickenlooper, a member of the Senate Commerce Committee, won his second and last term two weeks ago, leading Republican state Sen. Mark Baisley 61% to 35% on election night. While his seat was expected to go his way, eight seats won Democrats control of the Senate in last Tuesday’s midterm elections, in which data centers and the AI buildout was one of the most referenced issues that influenced voters’ decisions. His comments come as the buildout continues and as AI companies use their models to speed up their research. In September, more than 20 researchers, including Geoffrey Hinton and Yoshua Bengio, published a paper warning that automating AI research could set off an “intelligence explosion.” Alan Chan, one of its lead coauthors, said that valid safety mechanisms aren’t in place. Hickenlooper said he isn’t against the labs moving fast. “They are pushing as fast as they can. I understand that, and that’s good,” he said, referencing the international rivalry. “We want to make sure that our frontier AI is the best in the world because it has the potential to dominate the globe.” He said there are still ways to make sure the U.S. does that safely: for example, there are rules already on the books for other technologies. “We regulate nuclear weapons. We have regulations before an airplane can go into service,” he said. “We need to look at what are some of the fundamental safeguards and guardrails that we should put in place.” A global arms race Brady asked about Nvidia and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, following Jensen Huang’s resignation as Nvidia’s CEO last week after reports of an affair with an alleged Chinese spy. The Senate Banking Committee has asked Huang and Lutnick to testify next month. While Hickenlooper said his questions about the case were “not that pressing,” Hickenlooper, who is not part of the committee, said he wants to know the basics first. “What is our relationship to China, and how secure do we feel in sharing our technology with them at any level?” he said. “Because I don’t feel comfortable with that.” Hickenlooper backs the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act to help curb data centers. The permitting bill would speed approvals for energy projects and require data centers to pay for the grid upgrades built to serve them. The Senate voted 73-25 last week to begin debate on it, and President Donald Trump endorsed it. Hickenlooper said data centers should first guarantee there will be no loud noises or hazards and nuisances in communities. Under the bipartisan bill, the cost of new power lines and substations “will be completely borne by the data center.” He called the bill a compromise. Trump “doesn’t like wind. He doesn’t like solar,” Hickenlooper said, but the bill would put both on equal footing with natural gas. While the bill has limitations, he said, what it looks like now is one that is “much improved” from where it started. “I wish we could go further.” Hickenlooper read the midterm results as a test rather than a win for his party to bank. “It’s not a mandate,” he said. “I think it’s more of a to-do list, almost an audition.” Democrats, he said, have to show they can lower costs and add jobs. “When you’re trying to get a deal done, you’ve got to figure out who you’re negotiating with,” he said. “You got to see what’s in it for them and find a way that you can both benefit from the final agreement.” This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

events.title: JPMorgan Chase says temporary software bug is affecting consumer banking
events.summary: JPMorgan Chase on Monday said a "technical issue" was making some transactions take longer than usual for customers. A spokesperson for JPMorgan said the issue was not cyber-related and that it was not systemic. CNBC's Eamon Javers reported there was no indication of bad actors involved. JPMorgan Chase reported a "technical issue" that was affecting some consumer banking services Monday. The bank said a "temporary issue related to a software bug in on-premise hardware systems" was causing some customer transactions to take longer than usual, though it said customers can still access their accounts and funds. "There is no evidence it is cyber-related," a JPMorgan spokesperson said in a statement to CNBC. "This is not a systemic issue — other banks may have been impacted by slowness in transactions only to the extent that they were a party to a transaction with us," the spokesperson said. "We're working diligently to resolve this by the end of the day today." Still, other major banks were listed in outage reports as transactions between Chase and other institutions appeared to get held up. Users reported errors as early as 11:30 a.m. ET. A representative for U.S. Bank said that company was "not directly impacted. However, clients attempting to send or receive Zelle payments with another financial institution may experience transaction delays." Zelle is the peer-to-peer payments system backed by many of the largest U.S. banks, including JPMorgan. The outage reports come days after separate, widespread issues with Microsoft Outlook and communication systems used by air traffic control centers . — CNBC's Leslie Picker contributed to this report.

events.title: ‘Work on what people think is important.’ U.S. Steel’s CEO has advice for Democrats after the midterms: Focus on affordability, not court fights
events.summary: U.S. Steel CEO David Burritt wants to see Democrats use their congressional sweep to focus on what voters have been asking for: improving the cost of living and affordability, not spending the next two years fighting Trump in court. Speaking at the Fortune 500 Innovation Forum , Burritt said Democrats have an opportunity to respond to the economic concerns that have plagued the American electorate and drove voters to the polls, warning that a focus on political battles would undermine the party’s chances in the next election. He added that Democrats could find themselves in a difficult political position in the 2028 elections if they fail to address voters’ priorities. The midterm results shouldn’t be interpreted as an endorsement of the Democratic Party, but instead a warning for both parties that voters are dissatisfied, he said in a panel discussion with Oklahoma Governor Kevin Stitt and Fortune Executive Editor Lee Clifford. “They were sending a message to everybody: work on what people think is important. Let’s make things affordable,” Burritt said. Voters want affordability The Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress in the November midterm elections, a sweeping reversal of the political fortunes for Republicans and a rebuke to President Donald Trump. Democratic candidates repeatedly made affordability the centerpiece of their campaigns, arguing for cheaper groceries, healthcare, housing and everyday necessities. Housing and food accounted for 46.9% of average expenditures in 2025 as housing expenditures climbed 5.8% and food spending increased 4.6%, according to the Census Bureau’s Consumer Expenditure Survey released in October. A CBS News analysis of the election found that 89% of voters considered the cost of living a major or crucial factor in their congressional vote. But Trump was also a factor as well, with many voters treating the election as a referendum on him. According to the Associated Press’s Voter Poll, 39% to 60% of voters across age demographics used their vote to “show opposition” to Trump—compared to only 7% to 22% voting to show support. The poll also showed that 33% of the electorate viewed “the state of democracy” as its most important issue. A collision course with Trump The Democratic Party has signaled plans to investigate a range of issues, including Trump’s business interests, his administration’s immigration policies, the Justice Department’s actions, and the administration’s handling of the war in Iran. Congressional committees will gain the ability to issue subpoenas, compel testimony and demand documents once the new Congress convenes in January. But for Burritt, the danger is that Democrats will mistake their electoral victory for a mandate to pursue a political agenda rather than address the economic concerns that helped deliver their majority. Stitt offered a similar warning, saying Republicans had taken “a beating” in the midterms but that Democrats shouldn’t interpret the win as an endorsement of every policy on their platform. “Don’t go out and have this pendulum swing, don’t go start attacking the other side,” Stitt said. “I think the American people get turned off by that.” This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

events.title: Cyber giant Infoblox confirms security incident after hackers access ‘company information’
events.summary: Cybersecurity and automation giant Infoblox has confirmed a cybersecurity incident, during which hackers accessed company information through one of its technology vendors. Infoblox is a privately held cyber giant that provides companies cybersecurity and networking services, such as domain name resolution and identity and user access management. In a statement, a spokesperson for Infoblox told TechCrunch that the company is “investigating a security event involving unauthorized access to certain company information through a compromised third-party data migration vendor.” “We immediately activated our incident response procedures, took steps to contain the incident and are working with leading outside cybersecurity experts to investigate the facts, understand the scope and address any confirmed risks.” TechCrunch has learned that the data breach involves a vendor that provides SharePoint data migration services, according to a notification sent by Infoblox about the breach, two people with knowledge of the incident told TechCrunch. One of the people said sensitive customer data was taken in the breach. According to public internet records seen by TechCrunch, Infoblox hosts much of its files, emails, and infrastructure with Microsoft, including a SharePoint server, which TechCrunch confirmed is accessible through Infoblox’s single sign-on provider. SharePoint is web-based software that companies use to share and host internal files and documents. Infoblox has not named the third-party migration vendor that was hacked, but one person with knowledge of the incident said that Infoblox has terminated its work with the vendor. The company’s spokesperson did not comment on this, but added that the company has “no indication that any Infoblox products, cloud services, software updates or build-and-release processes were involved” in the breach. Infoblox would not say how many customers were affected by the incident, or if the company is aware at this time.
